name: Delta Lobe
desc: A river delta builds itself into a standing basin — sediment parcels walk the bed downhill, incise channels on the plain and settle at the mouth into bars that split the flow, so distributaries branch outward on their own; the lobe superelevates until the trunk avulses to a new one, and a slow rise and fall of sea level drowns and re-progrades the whole plain, so the basin never fills.

energy.doc: sediment load + channel incision vigour, and overall colour/contrast gain

scale.doc: magnification into the delta around x/y — 1 shows the whole basin, 2.6 crops to the distributary mouths

speed.doc: how fast the delta builds, avulses and drowns

density.doc: number of sediment parcels per step — thread count of the distributary network, and plume persistence

sealevel.doc: base sea level: 0 = a deeply incised subaerial plain, 1 = a drowned shelf with only the lobe tips showing

hue.doc: water hue anchor; rotates the chart inks with it

x.doc: view centre x (only bites when scale > 1)

y.doc: view centre y (only bites when scale > 1)

style.doc: aesthetic: bathymetric = survey chart, banded depth contours, buff plain; landsat = false-colour NIR, near-black water, cyan sediment plume, maroon vegetation; radar = abstracted dark plate with only the distributary skeleton glowing; ink = sumi tonal wash
